author: Athanasius of Alexandria
addressee: Monks practicing the solitary life, established in faith in God
occasion: Athanasius writes because some who hold the views of Arius are going around the monasteries to deceive the simple, and some who insist they do not hold Arian views nevertheless go down and pray together with them. At the exhortation of certain most sincere brothers, he writes to warn the monks against giving any occasion of scandal.
argument: Athanasius thanks the Lord for giving the monks faith in him, so that they too may have eternal life with the saints. He warns them about two dangers: those who hold the views of Arius and go around the monasteries to deceive the simple, and those who insist they do not hold Arian views yet go down and pray together with them. He urges the monks to shun those who openly hold impious views and to guard against those who share communion with the impious. If someone pretends to confess the right faith but is seen sharing communion with them, the monks should urge him to abstain from such habitual association; if he agrees, treat him as a brother, but if he stubbornly persists, reject him. By doing this they will keep their faith pure, and those who see them will benefit, fearing lest they be reckoned as impious and as holding those views.

outline.move: Athanasius greets the monks, warns them against Arians and those who pray with them, and gives practical instructions for preserving the pure faith and dealing with such persons.
